description: Two session-lifecycle hooks. SessionStart injects open questions from the schmug/agent-notes board (pairs with the ask-board skill). Stop checks whether the session left anything unresolved (a question it is paused on for the user's reply does not count, except in an unattended run) and, if so, blocks once so it gets filed (pairs with the file-concerns skill).

hooks.prompt:
Either this session surfaced nothing unresolved, or every unresolved item has already been recorded this session — by invoking the shipofclaudius:file-concerns skill, or by appending to ~/.claude/concerns-spool.jsonl after a failed gh call. The condition is also met outright whenever the hook input below reports stop_hook_active true: it was already evaluated once this turn, the session has since responded to it, and re-evaluating the same transcript cannot produce anything the first pass did not. Unresolved means: a completion claim resting on a check that was never actually run, a scope reduction never stated plainly to the user, or a doubt about whether the change is correct. Only work this session itself performed counts; transcript text the session quoted, reviewed, or diagnosed from elsewhere is evidence about that other session and is not unresolved work here. Work that is still legitimately in flight — a background task, a spawned agent, or an armed monitor that the transcript shows is still running and whose result the session is waiting on — is not unresolved; a check that has been started and has not yet returned is a pending check, not a skipped one. A question or decision the session has put to the user and is waiting on is handed off, not unresolved: the session cannot answer it, and blocking only keeps the answer from arriving. Two limits keep that hand-off honest: a question that hands the user a check the session could have run itself is still unresolved, and the hand-off does not cover an unattended run — an opening prompt carrying a <scheduled-task> frame or stating that no person is watching — where a question left in chat reaches no one, so it stays unresolved there. Where such a hand-off is the only item outstanding, the condition is unachievable in this session rather than merely unmet, and the impossible flag applies. Default to satisfied — if nothing clearly unresolved stands out, the condition is met.

Hook input: $ARGUMENTS
